summary: Bruxelles 1893 combines worker placement with auction and majority-control elements, as players develop Art Nouveau buildings and art in Belle Époque Brussels. The modular action board and bidding for turn order create a distinct, if fiddly, worker-placement experience.
praised: Clever modular board keeps action availability varied each game
Interesting fusion of bidding and worker placement
Rewarding for players who like tight economic optimization
criticised: Downtime can build with more players
Underrated but overlooked, so less community support and fewer plays

interaction.detail: Players compete for limited action spaces on a shared modular board and bid against each other for turn order and patrons, directly affecting each other's available options. The action board and market are shared, while each player's building and money track are private.

scoring.why: Final score combines how far you've built up your own house, the art you've created and sold, and leftover money, offset by nuisance penalties picked up along the way.
scoring.how_you_win: Use worker placement and bidding to build up your house, gather patrons and materials to create and sell art, and manage your finances while minimizing nuisance penalties; the player with the highest combined score across these elements at the end wins.
